item.name: 01 Health check

request.description:
PURPOSE

Confirms that the HIRELUME backend server is running and responding to requests.

HOW TO TEST

1. Make sure the HIRELUME backend server is running.
2. Send this GET request.
3. No authentication is required.
    

EXPECTED RESULT

```
Status: 200 OK

 ```

The response should contain:

``` json
{
"status": "ok",
"service": "hirelume-backend"
}

A successful response confirms that the backend is running correctly.


 ```

item.description:
PURPOSE

Contains the basic backend health check.

This confirms that the HIRELUME backend server is running and responding to requests.

TESTING NOTE

Run this first before testing the other endpoints.

item.name: 02 Authentication

request.description:
PURPOSE

Authenticates a recruiter and returns an access token that is required for protected recruiter endpoints.

HOW TO TEST

1. Open the Body tab.
2. Select raw.
3. Select JSON as the body type.
4. Enter the test recruiter login credentials.
5. Send the request.
6. Copy the value of "access_token" from the response.
7. Save the access token in the collection variable:
    

accessToken

Do not copy the entire response. Only save the value of "access_token".

EXPECTED RESULT

Status: 200 OK

The response should contain:

- access_token
- token_type
- user
    

The access token will be used to authenticate requests to protected endpoints.

PURPOSE

Confirms that the authentication token returned during login is valid and identifies the currently authenticated user.

HOW TO TEST

1. Run the Login request first.
2. Save the returned access_token as the collection variable:
    

accessToken

1. Open this request.
2. Go to Authorization.
3. Select Bearer Token.
4. Enter:
    

{{accessToken}}

1. Send the request.
    

EXPECTED RESULT

Status: 200 OK

The response should contain the authenticated user's information.

If the access token is missing, invalid or expired, the request should return an authentication error.

item.description:
PURPOSE

Contains the authentication tests for recruiter accounts.

These requests verify that a recruiter can log in and that the returned access token can be used to access protected backend endpoints.

TESTING ORDER

1. Login
    
2. Get Current User
    

The access token returned by Login is required for the protected requests that follow.

item.name: 03 Jobs

request.description:
PURPOSE

Creates an open recruiter job that will be used to test the public application flow.

HOW TO TEST

1. Run the Login request first.
2. Make sure the collection variable "accessToken" contains a valid recruiter access token.
3. Open this request.
4. Go to Authorization.
5. Select Bearer Token.
6. Enter:
    

{{accessToken}}

1. Provide the required job information in the request body.
2. Send the request.
3. From the successful response, copy the value of "public_token".
4. Save it as the collection variable:
    

publicToken

EXPECTED RESULT

The job should be created successfully.

The response should contain information including:

- Job ID
- Job title
- Job status
- Public token
- Job requirements
    

The created job should have:

status: open

The public_token will be used to test the public applicant flow.

item.description:
PURPOSE

Contains the recruiter job creation test.

The Create Job request creates an open job that is later used to test the public applicant flow.

TESTING NOTE

Run Authentication tests first because job creation requires a valid recruiter access token.

The public_token returned when a job is created is used by the application tests.

item.name: 04 Applications

request.description:
## Body

Use:

**Body → form-data**

Fields:

```
fullName
email
phone
consent
cv

 ```

For `cv`, select **File**.

PURPOSE

Tests the public applicant flow where a job seeker submits their personal information, consent and CV without creating a HIRELUME account.

HOW TO TEST

1. Run the Login request.
2. Run the Create Job request.
3. Save the returned public_token as the collection variable:
    

publicToken

1. Open this request.
2. Go to Body.
3. Select form-data.
4. Provide the following fields:
    

fullName  
email  
phone  
consent  
cv

1. Set the "cv" field type to File.
2. Select a test CV file.
3. Set consent to true.
4. Send the request.
5. From the successful response, copy the applicationId.
6. Save it as the collection variable:
    

applicationId

EXPECTED RESULT

Status: 201 Created

The response should contain:

- applicationId
- resultToken
- analysisStatus
    

The analysisStatus should be:

pending

"pending" is expected at this stage because the AI analysis worker has not yet been implemented.

The application should be saved successfully and the uploaded CV should be stored.

header.name: cache-control
header.info:
Postman added "Cache-Control: no-cache" as a precautionary measure to prevent the server from returning stale response when one makes repeated requests.

You can remove this header in the app settings or enter a new one with a different value.

header.name: postman-token
header.info:
The Postman-Token header appends a random UUID to every outgoing request. Postman adds this header for API developers to better debug requests sent and to ensure separate requests appear distinct to the receiving server.

You can remove this header in the app settings.

header.name: content-type
header.info:
The Content-Type header is added to help the server identify the media type of the request body that is present in this request.

Use the request body tab to control the value or to remove this header.
header.value: multipart/form-data; boundary=<calculated when request is sent>

header.name: content-length
header.info:
The Content-Length header was added to indicate to the server the size of the request body that is added to this request. Server uses this value to parse the request body accurately.

You can remove the header or enter a new one with a different value.

header.name: host
header.info:
The Host header is added to identify the domain name for which a request is being sent to the server. This header is implicitly sent by every HTTP client.

You can remove the header or enter a new one with a different value. It is most likely that without this header, your request will return an HTTP 400 error.

header.name: user-agent
header.info:
The User-Agent header is added to help the server identify Postman as the HTTP requesting application or client.

It is recommended that this header be sent, but you can remove the header or enter a new one with a different value.

header.name: accept
header.info:
The "Accept: */*" header is added to tell the server that Postman can understand and process all forms of response content types.

It is recommended that this header be sent, but you can remove the header or enter a new one with a different value.

header.name: accept-encoding
header.info:
The Accept-Encoding header is added to indicate to the server that Postman HTTP client supports a defined list of content-encoding or compression algorithms as response.

You can remove the header or enter a new one with a different value. Doing that may not accurately render the response within the app.

header.name: connection
header.info:
Postman added the Connection header to indicate the server to keep the underlying network connection open once the current response is received. This allows Postman to reuse the same connection for faster response times in subsequent requests to the same server.

You can remove this header or enter a new one with a different value, such as `Connection: Close` to control this behaviour.

request.description:
PURPOSE

Confirms that the same applicant email cannot submit more than one application for the same job.

HOW TO TEST

1. Run the "Submit Application + CV" request successfully first.
2. Use the same job.
3. Use the same applicant email address.
4. Submit the application again.
5. The other applicant information and CV can be provided again for testing.
    

EXPECTED RESULT

Status: 409 Conflict

The response should indicate that an application with the same email already exists for that job.

Expected message:

"An application with this email already exists for this job"

This confirms that duplicate applications are prevented.

PURPOSE

Confirms that an authenticated recruiter can access the CV attached to an application.

HOW TO TEST

1. Run the Login request.
2. Save the returned access_token as:
    

accessToken

1. Run the Submit Application + CV request successfully.
2. Save the returned applicationId as:
    

applicationId

1. Open this request.
2. Go to Authorization.
3. Select Bearer Token.
4. Enter:
    

{{accessToken}}

1. Send the request.
    

EXPECTED RESULT

The authenticated recruiter should be authorized to access the CV attached to the application.

The response is a file download rather than a normal JSON response.

Depending on Postman's display, the PDF may open in a viewer or appear as a file response.

This does not necessarily indicate an API failure.

PURPOSE

Confirms that an applicant cannot submit an application without giving the required consent.

HOW TO TEST

1. Make sure {{publicToken}} contains a valid open job token.
2. Open this request.
3. Use Body → form-data.
4. Provide:
    

fullName  
email  
phone  
cv

1. Do not provide valid consent.
2. Send the request.
    

EXPECTED RESULT

Status: 400 Bad Request

The response should contain:

"Consent is required before applying"

The application should not be created.

Method + URL

POST {{baseUrl}}/public/jobs/{{publicToken}}/applications

PURPOSE

Confirms that an applicant cannot submit an application without providing a CV.

HOW TO TEST

1. Make sure {{publicToken}} contains a valid open job token.
    
2. Open this request.
    
3. Use Body → form-data.
    
4. Provide:
    

fullName  
email  
phone  
consent

1. Do not attach a CV.
    
2. Send the request.
    

EXPECTED RESULT

Status: 400 Bad Request

The response should contain:

"CV file is required"

The application should not be created.

item.description:
PURPOSE

Contains tests for the HIRELUME public CV application flow.

These tests cover:

- Submitting an application with a CV
    
- Preventing duplicate applications
    
- Rejecting applications without a CV
    
- Rejecting applications without consent
    
- Authenticated recruiter access to an applicant's CV
    

TESTING ORDER

Run "Submit Application + CV" successfully before testing the related application validation and CV access requests.

The applicationId returned from a successful application is required for Recruiter CV Access.
